lessons.title: प्रवास: तिकीट आणि फलक
lessons.learn: At a Marathi station the destination comes before the ticket and takes -चे: पुण्याचे तिकीट. The timetable runs on the simple present — गाडी सुटते, पोहोचते — and बदल करणे is the verb for changing trains.

grammar.title: Ticket, platform, change
grammar.pattern: पुण्याचे दोन तिकीट द्या · गाडी किती वाजता सुटते? · कुठे बदल करायचा?
grammar.explain: The destination takes -चे/-ची before the ticket: पुण्याचे तिकीट, मुंबईची गाडी. A timetable states facts, so it uses the simple present: सुटते, पोहोचते, येते. बदल करणे is the standard phrase for a change of trains.

examples.en: Give me two tickets to Pune.
Do I get off at Satara?

dialogue.en: Give me two tickets to Mumbai.
The Mumbai train comes on platform three.
Where do I change?

dialogue.t: कल्याणला बदल करा, मग सरळ जाते.
dialogue.r: Kalyan-la badal kara, mag saral jate.
dialogue.en: Change at Kalyan, then it goes straight.

lessons.title: पुस्तकालय आणि अभ्यास
lessons.learn: A library runs on three words: सदस्यत्व, उधार and मुदत. The book borrowed stays the object of घेणे and is given back with परत करणे, and the deadline asks for the infinitive with -ायची: परत करायची मुदत.

grammar.title: Borrowing and returning
grammar.pattern: पुस्तक घेऊन जाऊ शकतो · परत करायची मुदत · शोधून काढणे
grammar.explain: शकतो / शकते says what one can do and needs no आहे after it. The infinitive with -ायची names what has to be done, so परत करायची मुदत is the date by which the book must come back. शोधून काढणे means to find something after looking for it.

examples.t: मी दोन पुस्तके घेऊन जाऊ शकतो का?
examples.r: Mi don pustake gheun jaau shakto ka?

lessons.title: सण आणि आमंत्रण
lessons.learn: An invitation is a polite imperative with an occasion attached: दिवाळीला आमच्या घरी या. With तुम्ही the imperative ends in -ा (या, बसा, घ्या), and the festival as a date takes -ला.

vocab.en: to visit, to pay a call

grammar.title: Inviting somebody
grammar.pattern: दिवाळीला आमच्या घरी या · फराळाला बसा · येणार का?
grammar.explain: The occasion takes -ला: दिवाळीला, गणपतीला, फराळाला. With तुम्ही the imperative ends in -ा, and an invitation is often framed as a question with -णार का? (येणार का?) so that the guest can refuse without refusing.

examples.en: Come to our house for Diwali.

mistakes.why: With तुम्ही the imperative ends in -ा; ये belongs to तू.
A festival as an occasion takes -ला.

dialogue.en: Are you coming for Diwali?

culture.text: A Maharashtrian kitchen changes with the ground under it: bhakri of jowar or bajri with a chutney in the Deccan, rice and coconut along the Konkan coast, peanuts and dry coconut in Vidarbha. Bhaji mandai mornings, misal for breakfast and ukdiche modak at Ganesh Chaturthi are the parts everyone knows. Tea, चहा, is the great leveller — a cutting is sold on every corner, and the invitation चहा घेऊ या closes more deals than a contract does.

reading.text: आज सकाळी मी भाजी मंडईत गेली. भाजीवालीने टोमॅटो आणि वांगी दाखवली. दर महाग वाटले, म्हणून मी थोडा भाव केला आणि शेवटी दोन किलो घेतले. मी पाठीमागच्या दुकानातून गरम मिसळ आणली. शेजारच्या दुकानात चहा मिळाला. घरी येताना मी नारळ आणि हिरवी मिरची घेतली. संध्याकाळी आईने भाजी केली आणि सगळ्यांनी एकत्र जेवण केले. हिशोब पाहिला तर पंधरा रुपये वाचले.
reading.gloss: This morning I went to the vegetable market. The vegetable seller showed me tomatoes and brinjal. The price seemed high, so I bargained a little and in the end took two kilos. From the shop behind I got hot misal. At the next shop I found tea. On the way home I bought a coconut and green chillies. In the evening my mother cooked the vegetables and we all ate together. When I looked at the accounts, fifteen rupees were saved.

listening.script:
स्नेहा: काका, भाजी किती रुपये किलो आहे?
विक्रेता: तीस रुपये किलो, मॅडम. ताजी आहे.
स्नेहा: थोडे कमी करा. पंचवीसला द्या.
विक्रेता: ठीक आहे, दोन किलो घ्या म्हणजे बरोबर होईल.
स्नेहा: चला, द्या. आणि मिरचीचे काय दर आहेत?
listening.gloss: Sneha: Uncle, how much is the vegetable per kilo? Seller: Thirty rupees a kilo, madam. It is fresh. Sneha: Make it a little less. Give it at twenty-five. Seller: All right, take two kilos and it works out. Sneha: Fine, give it. And what is the price of the chillies?

idioms.meaning: the morning market where produce is sold
roughly a kilo, a kilo or so
on account, to be paid later
the reckoning, the tally of what was spent

mistakes.why: Going to a city takes -ला; being in it takes -त. मुंबईला गेलो, मुंबईत राहिलो.
पैसे is plural, so it takes आहेत; आहे would make it one single rupee.
रुपये counted as a sum takes a plural verb: रुपये लागतात, रुपये पडतात.

task.title: Shop for vegetables in Marathi
task.instructions: Write a short market dialogue of six lines between a customer and a seller: ask the price per kilo, bargain once with कमी करा, settle on two kilos, and ask the price of one more thing. Then write down the account in one sentence with रुपये लागतात.
